# (PART) Foundations {-}

# The bioviz architecture {#architecture}

## Goals

`bioviz` was designed under three constraints:

1. **One coherent visual language.** Every module shares the same base theme,
   the same panel-size table, and the same figure-saving conventions. A
   reader should be able to recognise a `bioviz` figure without being told.
2. **Module independence.** Each module is a stand-alone R package under
   `packages/`. A user who only needs `survivora` can install just that
   package without pulling the rest of the suite.
3. **Composability over breadth.** The suite intentionally avoids re-implementing
   conventional plots (heatmap, volcano, KM curve, OncoPrint). Each module
   targets a specific *gap* in the conventional vocabulary.

## Layout

```
visualization_package/
├── DESCRIPTION              # umbrella bioviz meta-package
├── NAMESPACE
├── R/
│   ├── bioviz-package.R     # package-level docs
│   ├── bioviz-common.R      # shared theme, sizes, save helpers
│   └── bioviz-render.R      # bioviz_render_all()
├── packages/
│   ├── uncertainr/          # one R package per module
│   ├── provtrace/
│   ├── scalefusion/
│   ├── counterpath/
│   ├── intercapsule/
│   ├── densweave/
│   ├── clinladder/
│   ├── survivora/
│   ├── cohortprism/
│   └── riskweave/
├── scripts/
│   └── generate_all_figures.R
├── figures/                 # rendered demo PNGs (26 panels)
└── book/                    # this reference manual (bookdown)
```

## Module registry

The single source of truth for "what is in the suite" is the
`bioviz_modules()` data frame:

```{r eval=FALSE}
source("R/bioviz-common.R")
bioviz_modules()
#>      module      family                                      one_liner   n_figures
#> 1   uncertainr   uncertainty Uncertainty as a first-class visual element       3
#> 2   provtrace    provenance  Provenance and pipeline dependency...          2
#> 3   scalefusion  scale       Cross-scale semantic continuity...             2
#> ...
```

Both the master generator (`scripts/generate_all_figures.R`) and the table
of contents of this book are driven by this registry.

## Render pipeline

The end-to-end rendering pipeline is small enough to fit on one slide:

```
bioviz_render_all(output_dir)
   └── for module m in bioviz_modules():
         ├── source packages/m/R/m.R           (in an isolated env)
         ├── call m_save_demo(output_dir)      (per-module entry point)
         └── log success / failure
```

Per-module entry points always have the signature
`<module>_save_demo(output_dir)` and are responsible for writing the module's
curated figure set. This convention is what allows the suite to be rendered,
indexed, and documented uniformly.

## Versioning and dependencies

All ten modules are released together as `bioviz 0.2.0`. They share a tight
dependency set (`ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `scales`, `MASS`,
`ggraph`, `igraph`, `ggnewscale`, `grid`); no module pulls in additional
heavy dependencies.
